narrative_purpose: The cold-open anchor: the climax moment when the whole planet seems to act as one, a continent-wide surge of wildlife converging on the invaders — the image that forces the chapter's question of whether a planet can defend itself like a living body.
subject: A wide, smoke-lit Pandoran plain at the height of battle: from the treeline a vast coordinated surge of diverse wildlife — heavy six-legged beasts, packs of running predators, flying creatures stooping overhead — all pours in a single direction toward a distant, small line of human machines, the animals moving as one wave though nothing visible commands them; faint threads of bioluminescent light run through the ground and vegetation tying the scene into one network.
scene: A broad battlefield plain under a darkened, smoke-streaked sky, forest on one side surging with animals, the human line small and distant on the far side, Polyphemus faint above.
camera: A wide, slightly elevated establishing shot taking in the whole sweep of the charge from forest to distant enemy line.
light: Low, dramatic, smoke-filtered light; cool bioluminescent glow threading the forest and ground against the warmer haze of distant fire.
palette: Void-indigo and deep teal night, cool cyan bioluminescent threads, a restrained warm amber smear from distant fire and machines.
style: Painterly speculative-biology naturalist plate, cinematic and atmospheric, hand-painted texture.
detail_level: Crisp on the near surge of wildlife and the glowing ground-threads; the distant human line and sky softer and hazier.
composition: The wildlife wave sweeping from the lower-left/forest across toward the small distant enemy line at right, open smoky sky above for callout space.
consistency_notes: A canon-tier scene; keep the wildlife as a coordinated mass rather than individual hero creatures. Cool Pandora palette, from-within glow, dark enough beside and above the surge for callout labels.
